why: The same read-side claim, but archive.js allow-lists the dataset name to a bare name (no separators, no '..', no '@' operand syntax, no drive letters) and additionally requires both the resolved member root and the archive target to stay inside their directories, so no known member-path escape reaches tar.
proof: bench/exploits.js -> p6b submits three escaping shapes through the same dashboard route - a separator-bearing '..' segment, the bare '..', and a leading-'@' bsdtar operand - and asserts the handler rejects all three before any tar invocation and no tarball is produced.
neighbourNote: Identical claim text to p6; only the guards differ.
residualNote: This fixture's guard was defeated twice by adjudicators, each fix verified by reproduction: v1 rejected only separator-bearing names and the bare '..' defeated it (round-3 run 1); v2 added a resolved containment check but bsdtar's '@' operand semantics - resolve(data, '@..\\..\\X') stays inside data/ while tar strips the '@' and opens '..\\..\\X' - defeated it (round-3 run3b). v3 allow-lists the name. The tar-behaviour side remains host-dependent (measured with bsdtar 3.8.8; GNU tar's '@' semantics differ and are untested here).
